stories.headline: Fantasy baseball forecaster: Pitcher projections for the next 10 days
stories.summary: Keep up to date on who is pitching -- and how well they're expected to do -- with our forecaster, which provides a rolling 10-day outlook of every team's probable starting pitchers with game score projections.
stories.body:
Plan ahead in fantasy baseball with help from our forecaster projections. We will provide an updated preview of the next 10 days for every team, projecting the starting pitcher for each game and their corresponding projected fantasy points, using ESPN's standard scoring system (2 points per win, minus-2 per loss, 3 per inning, 1 per K, minus-1 apiece per hit or walk allowed, minus-2 per earned run allowed).

This page will be updated daily throughout the season, so be sure to check back often for the latest 10-day outlook.

For our 10-day projections for each team's hitting matchups, click here.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: Sleepers, breakouts and busts for 2026-27
stories.summary: Which fantasy basketball players are going to exceed expectations in 2026-27? Who will disappoint? Who is ready to take things to an elite level? Our experts list their picks.
stories.body:
Putting together a winning fantasy basketball roster starts with a great draft. And to have a great draft, you need to know which players to go after and which to avoid.

So which players will out-produce their average draft position (ADP) this season? Who will take their game to another level? And which players are the biggest risk to take a step backward?

Our fantasy basketball experts André Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Jim McCormick, Steve Alexander and Michael F. Florio offer their top sleepers, breakouts and busts for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Sleepers
Sleeper: A player who will far surpass his average draft position (ADP) in standard ESPN leagues.

Naz Reid, C/PF, Charlotte Hornets

Snellings: Reid was the NBA Sixth Man of the Year two seasons ago and had carved out a role with the Timberwolves as essentially a starter that had to come off the bench due to the depth of frontline talent in Minnesota. With his trade to the Hornets, Reid has the opportunity to show that he can produce even more as a full-time starter. Reid is an efficient scorer, a strong rebounder and defender, and one of the best 3-point shooting big men in the league. Particularly in category leagues, he is poised to return fantasy value far beyond where is selected in most drafts.

Alexander: Reid has always been one of my favorite under-the-radar players and he'll have new life this season, hopefully starting for the Hornets. I wish he was a better free throw shooter (72.8% for his career), but he only shot 1.6 of them per game last year, meaning the low volume won't hurt you too bad in that category. I expect all of his numbers to get a boost this year and he's played between 68 and 81 games in six straight seasons. The only concern is his usage rate while playing alongside Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller, but there should be enough to go around for Reid to eat.

Julius Randle, PF, Brooklyn Nets
Karabell: Randle's numbers and fantasy value fell quite a bit during two seasons with the Timberwolves, especially in rebounds, but there is little holding him back from high usage and big fantasy value with the barren Nets. Look at what Randle achieved statistically during his Knicks seasons, and expect a return to at least 24 PPG, 10 RPG and 5 APG for the other New York team, easily outproducing his tepid ADP, which always seemed out of line with his actual production.

Caleb Wilson, SF, Chicago Bulls
Florio: The No. 4 overall pick in this years NBA draft hit the ground running this summer. Wilson averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.5 blocks per game in the Summer League. That is after putting up similar numbers at North Carolina last year. He has apparently been turning heads in workouts with LeBron James, too. He will start at power forward on a Bulls team that has lots of opportunities up for grabs, both in terms of scoring and rebounding. Plus, with a current ADP of 96.3, he could be had in the double-digit rounds in some leagues. That is too much upside to pass at that price.

Anthony Black, PG/SG, Orlando Magic
McCormick: Black's career arc has been unique: once a lost lottery prospect, he took a clear step forward this past season. The big combo guard developed into a capable slasher who finished more than 70% of his attempts at the rim. With a growing playmaking repertoire and the potential to thrive in a better offensive scheme in Orlando, Black is primed to deliver value for fantasy managers.

Jaime Jaquez Jr., SF/SG, Milwaukee Bucks
Moody: Jaquez is worth keeping an eye on following his move to Milwaukee in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. He bounced back last season, averaging 15.4 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 4.7 APG in 28.3 minutes per game while shooting 50.7% from the floor. His improved ball-handling, shot creation and midrange game were a big part of that turnaround. Jaquez could start for the Bucks and should see more minutes alongside Tyler Herro. His ability to contribute in multiple areas gives him a chance to become a valuable fantasy contributor. I wouldn't be surprised if Jaquez sets career highs in multiple categories this season.

Breakouts
Breakout: A player who will leap into or close to the upper echelon of players at his position for the first time because of a dramatic increase in production compared with his previous seasons.

Walker Kessler, C, Los Angeles Lakers
Snellings: Kessler showed very strong per-minute and per-game stats in his last two seasons with the Jazz, averaging a solid double-double with more than three combined blocks and steals and shooting almost 70% from the field. However, injuries held him to only 63 of a possible 162 games in that span. This season, Kessler becomes the primary big man for a Lakers team featuring Luka Doncic. Doncic has made a career of making athletic big men look good on offense, and Kessler's defense and rebounding will be on full display. If he stays healthy, Kessler has top-40 potential in category leagues.

Cedric Coward, SF/SG, and Scotty Pippen Jr., PG/SG, Memphis Grizzlies

Karabell: Coward and Pippen should start at guard for a rebuilding franchise that will be vastly underrated on Opening Day. This team has exciting young talent! Coward averaged 13.6 PPG in only 25.8 MPG as a rookie, and he rebounds quite well for a guard and shoots well, too. He could average 20 PPG. Pippen, perhaps the starting point guard, boasts big upside for assists and steals. The Grizzlies have their young frontcourt with Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey, but this young backcourt, going far later in drafts, is quite underrated.

Brandon Miller, SF/SG, Charlotte Hornets
McCormick: The runway is paved for Miller's ascent; he'll be empowered with the playmaking and scoring opportunities set for a star. With usage set to spike and already elite shooting and fun defensive metrics on his side, Miller's run at prime Paul George production could begin as early as October.

Kel'el Ware, C, Milwaukee Bucks
Alexander: Ware has the kind of fantasy skill set that we dream about, specializing in blocks, threes and field goal percentage, with the ability to rebound, score and steal the ball, as well. He also improved his free throw shooting from 68.7% his rookie year to 74% last season. And while his role is undefined in Milwaukee playing behind Myles Turner, I simply believe Ware is the better player at this point. Hopefully, Taylor Jenkins will have more trust in Ware than Erik Spoelstra did last season and will play him a consistent 25 minutes per game. If that happens, look out.

Dereck Lively II, C, Dallas Mavericks
Moody: Lively can breakout if he can finally stay healthy. Injuries have limited him to just 98 games over three seasons, including seven last year. As a rookie, Lively averaged 8.8 PPG, 6.9 RPG and 1.4 BPG in only 23.5 MPG while shooting 74.7% from the floor. The Duke product is an excellent rim protector and pick-and-roll finisher who could benefit from playing alongside Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving. He'll share center minutes with Daniel Gafford, but if he can stay on the court and earn a larger role, double-digit rebounds and multiple blocks per game are within reach. That kind of production could push him into the upper tier of fantasy centers.

Ace Bailey, SF/PF, Utah Jazz
Karabell: The No. 5 pick in the 2025 NBA draft showed out nicely as a rookie, averaging 18.5 PPG. That is even more impressive when you factor in that he got off to a slow start. Once he was injected into the starting lineup, he showed his scoring ability that made him such a coveted prospect. As the season progresses his usage steadily climbed, reaching 26% in the final two months. His points, assists and rebounds per game all increased as well. I expect his playing time, usage and production to all take another jump in year two. He should be the focal point and top scoring option on a young Jazz team that could surprise this season.

Busts
Bust: A player who is expected to be a solid starter in standard ESPN leagues but will fail to live up to those expectations this season.

LeBron James, SF/PF, Philadelphia 76ers
Snellings: This pick is the difference between NBA impact and fantasy impact. LeBron signing with the 76ers was one of the major moves of the offseason and seemingly puts the 76ers in position to contend. However, when all five 76ers starters are healthy, LeBron projects as the fourth or even fifth option on offense. He showed last season with the Lakers that he was willing to take a smaller role behind two elite producers in Doncic and Austin Reaves, and when they all played together LeBron's fantasy production was low. In Philadelphia, playing with Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe it is hard to imagine LeBron producing fantasy stats anywhere near where his name recognition likely causes him to be drafted.

Florio: It pains me to have LeBron as a bust, but the truth is I am avoiding all the Sixers in fantasy this season. For a team with that much talent to work, everyone must sacrifice and take a step back volume wise. While there will be big games for James, I worry about consistency and what his usage will look like on a nightly basis. Plus, I suspect James (and Embiid) will have more rest days than fantasy managers can tolerate. While there are no signs of decline, he will soon be 42 years old. The Sixers will be fun to watch, but on someone else's fantasy team.

Ja Morant, PG, Portland Trail Blazers
Karabell: This isn't the first time Morant has been nominated as a fantasy bust, even as he finally comes at discount this year. After all, he has participated in 79 games over the past three seasons. It is difficult to help any team missing two-thirds of the games. Even if Morant plays in more than 62 games for the first time in six seasons, stop expecting big numbers. He averaged 19.5 PPG last season, only 3.3 RPG, and was an awful 3-point shooter. In addition, it is quite a crowded backcourt with Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday, though Morant can solve that issue by missing half the games.

Anthony Davis, C/PF, Washington Wizards
Moody: Davis is a bust candidate at his current ADP. He averaged 20.4 PPG, 11.1 RPG and 1.7 BPG in just 20 games last season before being traded to Washington, where he never played. Injuries continue to be a problem. Davis has missed at least 14 games in 10 of his 14 NBA seasons and has played more than 60 games just once in the past four campaigns. Now he'll have to share usage with Trae Young and No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa. Davis can still put up big numbers, but I'm not comfortable drafting him at his current ADP given his injury history and the changes in Washington.
Zion Williamson, PF/C, New Orleans Pelicans

Alexander: I've heard a lot of people talking about what a pleasant surprise Williamson was last season, but I'm just not feeling it. He played 62 games and averaged 21.0 points, but he didn't make a 3-pointer, and averaged just 5.7 rebounds and 0.5 blocks. The 62 games played represent the second-most he's played in six seasons, but I still don't trust him to play in more than 50 games this year. And even if he stays healthy and plays a full season, his fantasy game is weak and he'll continue to be overdrafted simply because of his name. Let someone else draft him.

Jakob Poeltl, C, Toronto Raptors
McCormick: Not only is his actual contract an albatross, it seems Poeltl's price in fantasy is also inflated. Drafted on average as the 26th center off the board, I'd clearly rather roster players such as Kel'el Ware, Derik Queen, Edey, and Nic Claxton, all of whom go later in drafts. There will be matchups that keep Poeltl off the floor in favor of Collin Murray-Boyles, further limiting the ceiling of a defensive specialist.

stories.headline: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 3
stories.summary: Can Baker Mayfield rebound? Are the Chargers doomed? Is the Eagles' new offense actually encouraging for Jalen Hurts? Get ready for Week 3 with seven takes.
stories.body:
Week 2 is in the books! It came with big upsets (Raiders over Chargers! Browns over Bucs!) and devastating injuries (such as Commanders QB Jayden Daniels and Giants QB Jaxson Dart). Week 3 feels as murky a future week as ever.

Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later in the week. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

This week, I'm starting with my concern for a big-ticket quarterback contract signed not even a month ago, my concern for one key AFC contender and my lack of concern for two others. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 3.

Jump to:

Bucs regret the Mayfield deal

Chargers to pick top-10 in 2027

Patriots offense is fine, everyone

Hurts is settling into Eagles' offense

Jaguars trenches will be postseason downfall

Henry won't solve Ravens' late-game issues

Donald's workout regimen paid off

Five extra inklings

I think ... the Buccaneers are already regretting that Baker Mayfield deal
Mayfield has not played well through the first two games of the season.

This does not mean he is a bad quarterback who is undeserving of a nice contract. Two game samples are, in a vacuum, barely above meaningless. (They're just meaningful enough that you should keep reading this column.) But it would have been nice to see how this season played out, to see if this two-game trend continued, before signing an extension.

Mayfield and the Buccaneers looked destined for a prove-it season before the Buccaneers "surprised" Mayfield with an eleventh-hour offer that clearly met his expectations. It is a three-year deal, as Mayfield wanted, though it's really a two-year deal with a $55 million team option in 2029. Still, at $55 million per year, Mayfield is making Matthew Stafford and Trevor Lawrence sort of money ... Joe Burrow and Josh Allen sort of money.

Mayfield's play has been decidedly below that level to start the season. Through two weeks, Mayfield is 29th among 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback and 27th in success rate. Of course, two-game samples are useless, so let's add last season. Since the start of 2025, Mayfield is 24th among 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback and 25th in success rate.

But last season was a down year. Mayfield played through a strained knee that he suffered in Week 2 and endured shoulder pain (non-throwing side) after a big hit in Week 12. His 2025 offensive coordinator, Josh Grizzard, was fired at the end of the season. So, let's throw in 2024 as well. Since the start of that season, Mayfield's career year with offensive coordinator Liam Coen, Mayfield is 13th in EPA per dropback and 13th in success rate. There he is, the guy the Bucs paid. We just had to go back a couple of seasons to find him.

But even including the 2024 season, we find some problems. A big part of Mayfield's success in that season, and in the seasons to follow, is how well he played when pressured. His dropback success rate (34.9%) is eighth; his first-down/touchdown rate (29.7%) is third behind Burrow and Brock Purdy.

But play under pressure tends not to be sticky. Pressured plays are either big wins (the passer beats the blitz with a deep throw) or disasters (the passer gets sacked), and that creates large swings in the outcome. Good play against pressure also relies heavily on athleticism. Mayfield has scrambled on 17.9% of his pressured dropbacks since the start of the 2024 season, second to Jayden Daniels. Mayfield's numerous 2025 injuries reflect his toughness, but they also reflect his playstyle. He gets sacked a lot (22.8% pressure to sack ratio, eighth highest) and takes more hits on scrambles down the field. It is reasonable to expect Mayfield's effectiveness against pressure to decline with age and accumulated hits; he's 31 years old! I'd argue it already has.

This season, Mayfield's scramble rate has almost halved (9.2%) as the Buccaneers have prioritized throws behind the line of scrimmage, but his ability to escape is also underwhelming, leading to a 9.2% sack rate.

Here's one of three sacks he took against the Browns. Cool concept here on third-and-7 from new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, who motions receiver Emeka Egbuka into the bunch to create a natural pick for Chris Godwin Jr. to get into the slant. The Buccaneers get the hoped-for man coverage. This ball should be out to Godwin immediately.

Mayfield is aggressively climbing the pocket despite the fact that there's plenty of room to stand and throw, and accordingly, he's too late to get the ball to Godwin by the time he reaches a throwing platform. Watch safety Ronnie Hickman, meant to rob the middle of the field, burn right by Godwin and give Mayfield hot pursuit; Hickman knows the scouting report on the quarterback. As Mayfield tries to escape, Hickman hawks him down.

Here's another simple one from Week 1 against the Bengals. Rookie wideout Ted Hurst III has a vertical route to the bottom of the screen, and the single-high safety is on the opposite hash when Mayfield drops back. A veteran quarterback needs to land on his back foot and send this throw, beating the deep safety to the spot by pulling that vertical route outside the numbers. Not an easy throw, but one a $55 million quarterback should be expected to attempt. Instead, he hitches, double-clutches and gets sacked

Mayfield's attempts breakdown has become worryingly polarized through two games of the Robinson offense. A harrowing 37.1% of Mayfield's pass attempts are behind the line of scrimmage, more than all quarterbacks save for Aaron Rodgers and Patrick Mahomes. But 16.1% of his throws go more than 20 yards downfield, as well; that's fifth highest in the league. Such a spray chart is unhealthy. It indicates a quarterback is uncomfortable testing coverage and either checks it down in front of all defenders or sails it deep beyond all defenders.

Again, this is a small sample. Seven of these eight deep throws came in Week 2 against the Browns, and the lack of success had more to do with miscommunications than anything else. If you're looking for a sunny side in the Buccaneers' offense through two games it's that clearing up those little mistakes should lead to big downfield connections.

This is why the Buccaneers might regret that Mayfield deal. Not because his bad play through two games is written in stone, but because they could have collected a season's worth of additional data to inform their contract decision, and at little cost. What was Mayfield going to demand if he had a good year? Maybe $60 million instead of $55 million? Actual guarantees in 2029?

These are peanut problems compared with the larger issue: Mayfield is a late-career breakout who relies heavily on his athleticism and accordingly is on a shorter time horizon than most quarterbacks over 30. He also plays an inherently erratic style, and Robinson has had little success tamping that down through two weeks. I enjoy when Mayfield is at his best and look forward to seeing it again, but paying for peaks makes the valleys difficult to endure. The Buccaneers likely never had a better alternative than paying Mayfield a sizable veteran contract, but I sure would have liked to turn every stone before I consigned myself to that path.

I think ... the Chargers will pick in the top 10 of next year's draft
I can't name 10 teams worse than the Chargers (0-2) through two weeks. I'm not even sure if I can name five.

There is nothing about the Chargers that works right now. They remind me of the Nathaniel Hackett-led Broncos in 2022. I have no idea what they're working on at practice throughout the week.

One season after the interior offensive line made football untenable in Los Angeles, general manager Joe Hortiz and head coach Jim Harbaugh have failed to improve it an inch. The Chargers' guard-center-guard trio, which featured a Week 1 rotation between Kayode Awosika and Trey Pipkins III, remains one of the worst in the NFL. Even worse, both star tackles, Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt, look like players affected by their 2025 injuries (Alt, in particular).

In theory, the Mike McDaniel offense can mitigate the effect of poor pass protection by getting the ball out fast. But that hasn't happened. Justin Herbert is constantly dropping his eyes and climbing the pocket the moment he hits his back foot. At times, the throwing windows are not there, as the Chargers' receivers (save for Ladd McConkey) struggle mightily to create separation. At other times, Herbert is unwilling to rip it.

The Chargers' offensive issues extend to the running game. McDaniel was elite here with the Dolphins last season. Their 13.5% explosive rush rate on running back carries led the league. The Chargers are down to 9.1%, and their 0.2 yards before contact per carry is third worst among offenses. The interior cannot generate vertical displacement, and second-year running back Omarion Hampton is suffering for it; he has been hit behind the line of scrimmage on 54.2% of his carries, seventh worst among league backs. He has also made a fair share of nosedives into contact when patience would have served him well, and has fumbled twice as a result.

The fumbles bring up something else. The Chargers are barely playing professional football. "Chargering" once meant heartbreaking losses in end-of-game collapses. These Chargers start the game collapsing. They have 13 offensive penalties this season (second to the Panthers). The Chargers have fumbled the ball seven times (somehow tied with the Packers for the most through two weeks), including six in Week 2 against the Raiders. One such fumble was a mistimed snap/motion combo on third-and-inches that forced a punt. The Chargers have lost 42 percentage points worth of win probability through turnovers in two games, behind only the Patriots. The Chargers are blowing assignments in pass protection and allowing free rushers; Herbert has a quick pressure rate of 21.5%, seventh highest among all quarterbacks.

Now, on to the defense.

The high preseason expectations for the offense have overshadowed the early disappointments for the defense in its first two games post-Jesse Minter. Sure, it's not all bad under first-year defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary. The Chargers are preventing explosives (9.1% explosive play rate allowed) at a clip well above league average, which is the point of this defensive structure. But they're suffering a paper-cut death.

Despite facing quarterbacks Jacoby Brissett and Kirk Cousins, the Chargers have allowed the ninth-highest passing success rate among league defenses, and it should be worse: They have a league-leading six opponent drops working in their favor. The defense is still forcing tight windows by driving on routes from deep-zone alignments, as they did with Minter -- only the Bills have forced more tight-window throws, per NFL Next Gen Stats -- but the Chargers' defensive backs are too small to affect the catch point across the board. Quarterbacks throwing into tight windows against the Chargers are 10-for-13 with a 148.7 passer rating. Since the start of last season, tight-window attempts have averaged about 4.3 yards. The Chargers, though, are allowing 10.3 on average through two games this season.

Even if the Chargers improve in that area, it might not matter as they face a gauntlet of opponents in the next two months: at Buffalo in Week 3, at Seattle in Week 4 (presumably with Sam Darnold back), vs. Denver in Week 5, at Kansas City in Week 6, at the Rams in Week 8 after a Week 7 bye, vs. Houston in Week 9 and at Baltimore in Week 10.

What's a best-case scenario through that stretch? Winning three of seven would be a miracle -- they won't be favored in one of those games, barring major injury -- and would give the Chargers a 3-6 record. By then, the season might already be dead.

A record of 2-7 (or worse) feels a lot more likely, and that is still charitable. Through two weeks, the Chargers look as if they've never practiced together. Herbert lets bad plays spiral and is more visibly skittish, frustrated and confused than I can remember seeing him. Going back to the playoff loss to the Patriots, this is the worst three-game stretch of his career. If the Chargers implode, they risk more than an embarrassing season and a top-10 pick. They risk losing the trust of their franchise quarterback and watching that essential keystone of a Super Bowl contender fracture permanently.

I think ... the Patriots' offense is fine, though I understand why people think otherwise
Weird things are afoot in New England. Coach Mike Vrabel was asked after the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers about his concern level regarding Drake Maye and the offense, to which Vrabel responded that he wasn't going to let questions about the offense ruin his Sunday and his enjoyment of the win.

The Patriots (1-1) had an extremely regular and unremarkable day on offense against the Steelers (1-1). New England's success rate of 45.3% was almost exactly its average success rate since the start of last season (45.4%). Same for yards per play: 6.2 on Sunday and 6.1 since the start of the 2025 season.

The only thing worth remarking on in New England is the turnovers. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson fumbled on the first drive, reawakening the sleeping dragon of his ball-security issues and opening the door for TreVeyon Henderson, who was active and healthy after missing Week 1, to hit a 39-yard touchdown run and get more snaps than Stevenson (32 to 15) the rest of the way.

The second giveaway was a Maye interception, his fourth pick of the year. Jack Sawyer came free on the loop, hurrying Maye into a challenging flat-footed throw. He's throwing this route only because linebacker Patrick Queen's back is turned, but Queen flipped his body and located the football in the air, which is not a given for NFL linebackers. Two of Maye's three picks in Week 1 against the Seahawks were terrible reads and bad throws, but this one Sunday was a good defensive play to create, then capitalize on a bad offensive play. It happens sometimes!

New England scored only 13 offensive points, and these two drives ended on turnovers inside the Steelers' 35. Maye was sacked three times against a deep defensive line that was wreaking tons of havoc, and he created more positives with his legs than allowed negatives in the pocket. Even without receiver A.J. Brown (high ankle sprain) and battling rain, the Patriots still found explosives in the air. There was a scramble-drill teardrop to Romeo Doubs on third-and-5 and a high-corner route to Eli Raridon -- a very similar play to the pick Maye threw, down to the interior pressure. It was a fine day!

But the discourse about the Patriots that centers on schedule strength and team-level performance has become distilled and concentrated into reactive Maye referendums. He played great last season (MVP runner-up). It doesn't mean he's as good as other MVP winners, such as Lamar Jackson and Mahomes. We need to see more to know that. It doesn't mean he'll always play at that level; ask MVP winner Matthew Stafford about Week 1 against the 49ers. This weird scrambling to rip the mask off Maye and reveal a so-so quarterback, similar to an episode of "Scooby-Doo," feels unwarranted and ultimately fruitless.

The Patriots have faced a brutal run of opponents. In the playoffs, they faced the defenses of the Chargers, Texans, Broncos and Seahawks. This season started with a Seattle rematch. Because so much was written about Maye's easy schedule in 2025, this stretch has become the cleansing light of truth in the world of knee-jerk discourse (this is who Maye really is). The better explanation is far simpler: Every quarterback looks worse when they play truly top-tier defenses. The truth of Maye is somewhere in the middle, and the truth will change over time, especially as Brown gets reintroduced to the offense and as Maye gains more playoff experience.

New England has a very interesting test in Week 3 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Trevor Lawrence has been surging at quarterback in the same way Maye did through the 2025 season. After watching Broncos defensive tackle Zach Allen terrorize the Jaguars' interior, the Patriots should feel good about their defensive matchup against Jacksonville on paper. Christian Gonzalez just put DK Metcalf to bed for four quarters. Will Gonzalez do the same to Brian Thomas Jr.? Or can the Patriots find a way to get him over Parker Washington in the slot?

But there's no doubt that the margins will be thinner against Jacksonville, even if the defense has a good day. The Steelers' offense lacked the teeth to punish the Patriots for their two giveaways. Drew Lock and the Seahawks barely pulled it off with three picks. The Jaguars won't struggle nearly as much, and the injuries are piling up in New England, as starting right guard Mike Onwenu (broken right ankle), tight end Eli Raridon (thigh), safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) and edge Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder) all left the Pittsburgh game early.

This is a game for Maye to produce more than an average day on offense and demonstrate the floor-raising efficiency that characterized much of his 2025 (and 2024) season. It has been a brutal run of defenses through the 2025 postseason and into 2026, and Jacksonville offers a bit of a reprieve. It's a gut-check game for New England.

I think ... Jalen Hurts is settling into the Sean Mannion offense
At a team level, I do not love what I'm seeing from the Eagles' offense. The offensive line looks worse even than it did in 2025, and the running game is suffering as a result -- fifth-lowest yards before contact per rush among all teams through two weeks. For the amount of money poured into that unit, that's scary. Hopefully, guard Landon Dickerson comes back from his injury looking back to form, but we haven't seen that form in a while; same for center/guard Cam Jurgens. I'm not holding my breath.

But Hurts' Week 2 performance against the Titans was about as good of a game a quarterback can have with a dead-in-the-water rushing attack. Hurts had nine third-down conversions in this game, the most single-game third-down conversions he has had. With no running game, Hurts averaged 7.9 yards to go on third down, well above his career average, and still got big gains in the air, converting three third-and-12 or longer downs (the most in a game in his career).

Perhaps most notable of these late conversions was the first one. Hurts hits an intermediate in-breaker to Dontayvion Wicks between the layers of the defense.

This throw has been the golden goose of the Sean McVay/Kyle Shanahan offense and the bane of Hurts' existence in the NFL. Since the 2021 season, only 7.3% of Hurts' throws have been 10 to 22 yards downfield and between the numbers. Among 44 quarterbacks with at least 1,000 dropbacks, that ranks 43rd, above only Russell Wilson.

One of the key objectives of the Mannion era in Philadelphia has been opening this area of the field. It's just one play, but to see Hurts willingly trigger on a throw like this is a significant sign of growth.

There are other objectives to Mannion's offense: get under center more and run more play-action. These we will charitably call "works in progress." Hurts had six snaps under center in play-action against the Titans after only two against the Commanders in Week 1, and that's still lagging well behind the league's ever-increasing usage of under-center dropbacks. He went 3-of-6 for 27 yards against Tennessee, not exactly gangbusters numbers.

But there is evident comfort and intent. Hurts ripped a deep outbreaker to DeVonta Smith, who was so, so good Sunday, against leverage, and then was just a beat late on a huge corner route to Smith in the end zone. As Hurts gets faster and more comfortable in the offense, the hope is that he'll eliminate some of these additional hitches and create more YAC opportunities by hitting throws before the sideline.

The Eagles have yet to log a convincing win against two inferior opponents, and their overall team health has me pretty dubious. But what a refreshing change of pace from most seasons when the Eagles were a super team, and we were debating how much credit Hurts deserves. He was, emphatically, one of the Eagles' best individual players against the Titans and the reason Philadelphia won the game. And his contributions were far from perfect, too. With better timing, he could reach another level in this new-look offense.

The Eagles (2-0) face the Bears (1-1) on "Monday Night Football" in Week 3 (8:15, ESPN/ABC), another light defensive test. There's a real opportunity here for a confidence-building game in the passing attack before the Rams in Week 4. My overall expectations for the Eagles' offense will remain tempered until I see the line and the running game return to form, but if Hurts can use his arm to guide them to wins through September and into October, they'll have time to iron out their rushing issues.

I think ... the Jaguars' trenches will be a problem come playoff time
The Jaguars are 1-1. They are also the sole leader of the AFC South through two weeks; the Colts, Texans and Titans are a combined 0-6. Good stuff.

The Jaguars are also really good. They went punch for punch with the Broncos in Denver -- not an easy ask -- and even in a loss, stacked another tremendous Trevor Lawrence day in the emphatic Liam Coen-led rebuild of their young quarterback. Lawrence hit a couple of defenders in the hands, but that's the cost of doing business when you're ripping downfield throws with reckless abandon. I love the aggressiveness in that passing game.

I do not love when Lawrence has to hold the ball. One of the first objectives that Coen and GM James Gladstone had when they took over the Jaguars was a reinvigoration of the offensive line. In the 2025 offseason, they signed offensive linemen Robert Hainsey and Patrick Mekari and drafted Wyatt Milum. Every job was up for grabs, and that's how Cole Van Lanen, who was a backup, ended up as the starting left tackle and eventually earned a nice extension.

In 2026, the Jaguars were willing to shuffle again. They flipped Van Lanen to the right side and moved 2023 first-round pick Anton Harrison to the blindside. Third-round rookie Emmanuel Pregnon out of Oregon won the starting left guard job over Wyatt Milum; Ezra Cleveland, who spent 2025 at left guard, has been moved to the right.

Maybe all of this shuffling will prove the ideal alignment. And I certainly don't want to grade Pregnon on his second career start. But the Jaguars' line struggled against Denver. Zach Allen and Nik Bonitto had four pressures apiece. Allen (and his fellow interior rushers) found fast wins, which forced Lawrence to get rid of the ball before he could pick his matchup to exploit. Lawrence was pressured on 45.2% of his dropbacks and to great effect: He completed 33.3% of his pressured throws and 76.5% when unpressured. He had Denver's secondary beat when he had time.

Watch how often the Broncos get an early one-on-one win and a second, converging rusher on these reps. They were able to pincer Lawrence in the pocket by winning across the board. This wasn't just one weak offensive lineman they exploited; it was a comprehensive rush.

Compare and contrast this with the other side of the ball. The Jaguars' pass rush needs Josh Hines-Allen to excel; it doesn't have a duo, let alone a deep group. Former 2022 No. 1 pick Travon Walker is a wonderful pocket pusher who can clean up sacks with his huge tackle radius, but he isn't a high-pressure player; his pressure rate since the start of last season is 10.3%, well below the league average for edge rushers (12.6%). Defensive tackle Arik Armstead (8.5% pressure rate) is just above league average for interior players (7.6%). The Jaguars have some cool rotational players (Dennis Gardeck and Danny Striggow), but their base four-down rush isn't playoff-caliber.

This game against the Broncos served as a great example. Jacksonville had only a 19.4% pressure rate, less than half the 45.6% the Chiefs had in Week 1. And despite what you might expect, it was the Jaguars who blitzed more, at a 45% clip. Of their five second-half pressures, a half in which the Jaguars mostly led, four came on blitzes. Only one was in a four-down rush.

Hines-Allen was shut out in this one, finishing with 24 pass-rush snaps and 0 pressures. The Broncos' Garett Bolles had an All-Pro day at left tackle, and Walker's couple of wins against Mike McGlinchey weren't enough to even the scales. The Jaguars' defensive tackles have five pressures on 106 pass-rush snaps through two weeks. Consider the defensive tackle duos to recently make Super Bowl runs: 2025 Seahawks' Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams; 2025 Patriots' Milton Williams and Christian Barmore; 2024 Eagles' Milton Williams and Jalen Carter. The Jaguars aren't even halfway to a presence like that.

It's never too early to look to the playoffs, certainly not for the Jaguars, who have a quarterback and an offense worthy of those aspirations. But the first teams I distrust in the playoffs are the ones that lose the trench battles. The book isn't written, but after two weeks, I'm worried the Jaguars fall below that bar. A premier defensive tackle at the trade deadline, á la last season's Quinnen Williams, might be a godsend.

It's not too early to look to Week 3, either. The Jaguars get the Patriots at home in a game they should win. But the Patriots have a ferocious defensive tackle duo in Barmore and Williams, a good enough group to break the Jaguars' passing attack in the pocket, similar to what Denver did. Patriots left tackle Will Campbell might not be Bolles, but the best spot to beat the Patriots' offensive line is on the interior, and I'm not sure Jacksonville has the players for that.

I think ... the Ravens' late-game problems won't be solved with more Derrick Henry touches
They'll be solved only with some sort of ritual sacrifice to Vince Lombardi.

The Ravens (1-1) lost their seventh game since the start of the 2021 season in which they held a lead of at least 11 points. That leads the league, but we can make it worse. If we look exclusively for games in which the Ravens, at any point, had a win probability of at least 88%, we find that they have lost 11 such games, three more than the next-closest team.

(Did I have to drop the threshold from 90% to 88% to force this Sunday's Saints loss into the sample? Yeah, but I had to. And that's the point.)

For years, Baltimore fans blamed these losses on head coach John Harbaugh, but he's no longer here, so a new vent must be found. What has been particularly frustrating in recent history are their late-game losses in which they had Henry, but failed to use him. Henry is a uniquely taxing runner, given his size and strength, and has historically been a better second-half and fourth-quarter runner as the opposing defense gets winded. Yet, since the start of the 2024 season, the Ravens have four losses in which they've cleared that 88% win probability threshold. Sunday's loss to the Saints is one of them.

The issue is that, though we might rush to cry "same old Ravens" at this disappointing result, the game against the Saints isn't really the sort of tectonic collapse we've associated with the Harbaugh Ravens. The Saints had the ball after halftime and were trailing by eight points, and never did the deficit become wider than that. New Orleans tied the score on a 2-point conversion with 9:42 remaining in the fourth; still a lot of game left.

Compare that loss with the real Ravens' disaster classes. In Week 16 of last season, the Ravens led the Patriots 24-13 with 12:50 left then lost in regulation as Maye guided two consecutive touchdown drives. In an unreal season opener in 2025, the Ravens led the Bills by 15 points with 11:42 left in the fourth before losing that game in regulation, too. That was the game in which Henry had a fourth-quarter fumble, something he never does, to put the Bills in position to pull within one score.

The Ravens never entered salt-the-clock mode against the Saints because they never got to that game state. They weren't up by two scores in the fourth quarter. They lost Zay Flowers (and Ja'Kobi Lane) at wide receiver, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley left the game in the third quarter (toe) after struggling against Chase Young. The Saints were also run-blitzing in the second half in an effort to take Henry out of the game plan, and coordinator Declan Doyle had some good calls to beat those looks, but pass protection failed across the board.

I wrote in Week 1 that the game against the Colts might be peak for the Ravens' offense, at least for a while, and I still believe that. Center is very much a weak point, and the tight end room isn't as good of a blocking group as it needs to be for the running game to shine independent of the opponent. The passing attack is, obviously, very Flowers-centric, as the receiver room is thin behind him.

Could the Ravens have funneled more runs to Henry? Sure. The larger issue is that they never put the Saints to bed in the bulk of the game; the Ravens were too lacking in talent on offense, and defensively, their dam burst as the Saints made second-half adjustments. I still like the Ravens from a season-long perspective, but this is a growing team. The Ravens get an unbelievable soft stretch of defenses over the next three weeks (Cowboys, Titans and Falcons) with a potential return of Flowers. This is good soil from which to grow confidence and cohesion on offense.

I think ... Aaron Donald's ridiculous retirement workout regimen has paid off
Thirty-two snaps? For a 35-year-old defensive tackle who hasn't played in 2½ years? I really can't believe it. Even if you remind me that this guy is a supervillain athlete, I still would have guessed 15, maybe 20 snaps in his debut game.

Only three defensive tackles at least 35 years old have taken at least 30 snaps in a game since the start of last season: John Jenkins, Calais Campbell and Cameron Heyward. Donald could have easily gotten to 40 if forced to contribute in the second half; he took four snaps in the fourth quarter.

The Rams didn't give Donald long strings of plays. They subbed their lines consistently, especially as they used four- and five-man fronts to combat various personnel groupings from the Giants. So, I still have conditioning questions, though those will exist with any big man playing at his age; it's hard to keep that engine humming for four quarters.

The Giants also wanted to test that motor, and they went tempo in the third quarter when Donald was on the field, though they weren't good enough on offense to pick up first downs and keep him trapped.

But how did Donald look with fresh legs? I was impressed. He's still quick as a cat off the line of scrimmage. Watch here on the final play of the first quarter. The Giants are trying to pin him with the right tackle and pull the center and guard around the block. Donald is so quick upfield that he forces the center (John Michael Schmitz Jr., No. 61) to take a wide path around his disruption (and he gets a little tug on the jersey as a bonus) while running back Cam Skattebo is accelerated by the blitz behind. The timing of the play is ruined.

Late in the first half, the Giants ask tight end Isaiah Likely to block down on Donald so they can run a puller in behind. This is a very silly idea. Donald again gets too far upfield and disrupts the puller, and Najee Harris is forced to burrow his head into the line of scrimmage and eat a TFL.

As long as that first step is still kicking, Donald will be a problem for opposing offenses. Next Gen Stats had Donald with a 0.75-second get-off in this game, tied for the third-fastest get-off for a defensive tackle in a game this season. That sort of upfield disruption, even if it comes with fewer finished rushes and sacks, or comes on a lower snap count, still matters a great deal.

Were this a random game in 2023, I'd call it a bad performance for Donald's pass-rushing presence. He ate a lot of double-teams, which opened up other rushers. But he struggled to separate from offensive linemen and create pressure on the quarterback. He had only one pressure on the day, which occurred late in the fourth quarter, when the Giants were down by 22 and in desperation mode. In the Next Gen Stats era -- from 2016, 134 regular-season and playoff games -- Donald has had only one pressure in eight games. This was a rare sight.

I'd be worried about that if it weren't a weird game script: Jaxson Dart out (knee), good Giants offensive line, no real reason to play Donald in the fourth quarter. The pressures will come as Donald gets back into the flow of pass rushing against real offensive linemen. That's the sort of thing that no shirtless Instagram workout can really replace.

Five things I might think

I might think ... absolutely nothing about the Carolina Panthers. Through two weeks, there is no team from which we should draw less certain conclusions than from the Panthers. In games against the Bears in Week 1 (lost 59-37) and the Falcons in Week 2 (won 34-3 against backups Cooper Rush and Jack Strand), there were absurd game scripts and ridiculous plays. I think there's a chance the Panthers' offense is pretty good (receivers look great), but I'm holding no strong opinions about Carolina, and after Week 3's game against the Browns, I'll likely feel much the same.

I might think ... the Packers' season is chalked. The Packers needed a great punt return from Skyy Moore and an Aaron Glenn end-of-game clock management transgression to get to overtime against the Jets (1-1) and save themselves from an 0-2 start. The Packers aren't in as dire straits as the Chargers, but Green Bay lost two starters to injury -- WR Jayden Reed and RT Zach Bako-Bewele -- and the line is already thin on starting-caliber players. Kaleb Johnson looked fine, but not enough to save their running game. If Lukas Van Ness can keep his form when Micah Parsons comes back from last season's torn ACL injury, their defense might keep them in playoff contention. They should go 2-1 with a Thursday night win over the Falcons, but I have little to trust in Green Bay through two weeks.

I might think ... the Commanders will have a new starting quarterback in 2027. I'll know what I actually think when we get real news about Jayden Daniels' elbow injury. He's getting imaging and multiple opinions over this week. But Daniels missed 10 games last year. If he misses 15 games this year, I don't see how the Commanders don't consider a young, developmental investment in QB2. They won't give up on Daniels. If he's healthy, he'll get the 2027 Week 1 start, and they'll do everything they can to recapture his 2024 magic (and availability). But the Commanders will have to have a better long-term view at QB2 than Mariota. Anthony Richardson Sr., anyone?

I might think ... we should all band together and vote Dexter Lawrence II for Defensive Player of the Year, no matter his stat sheet. The highlight reel of Lawrence's run-stuffs against the Texans is an absolute sight to see. It's better than the Bengals could have dreamed of. Jonathan Allen is also feasting as a pass rusher next to Lawrence. It's exactly what the Bengals were paying for when they traded the 2026 10th pick to the Giants for Lawrence. The Bengals' offense hasn't been gangbusters through two weeks, but the defense is winning games. Give him the trophy.

I might think ... the Bears beat the Eagles on "Monday Night Football" with Tyson Bagent at quarterback. Bagent is a pretty good backup. The Bears' run game is vicious and took Vic Fangio's defense for a ride last season. The Eagles' run game is nonexistent right now given their offensive line injuries, and starting tight end Dallas Goedert is on injured reserve. This just feels like a spot for the Bears to rally.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool, Arsenal, Man City in race for Feyenoord defender
stories.summary: Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right back Givairo Read, but face competition from Arsenal and Manchester City. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Feyenoord right back Givairo Read has caught the eye of Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City, while Manchester United are monitoring Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy and Vålerenga's 15-year-old winger Gabriel Rajkovic. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are monitoring Feyenoord right back Givairo Read, but face competition from Arsenal and Manchester City, according to TEAMtalk. The 20-year-old Netherlands U21 international has registered four assists in seven Eredivisie appearances this season, with all three clubs continuing to track his progress following summer interest. A January move remains an option depending on formal approaches, after Nottingham Forest and AS Roma previously submitted offers of around €20 million that came to nothing.

- Manchester United are monitoring Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy as they assess attacking options ahead of January, TEAMtalk reports. The 30-year-old is being considered as an experienced option should Joshua Zirkzee depart, while United remain committed to Benjamin Šeško despite his recent injury issues. Dortmund are reluctant to let Guirassy leave, but his contract has than two years remaining, which could force their hand. Meanwhile, The Sun reports that United are targeting Vålerenga's 15-year-old winger Gabriel Rajkovic as a replacement for JJ Gabriel.

- Barcelona are monitoring Athletico Paranaense center back Arthur Dias, as per Mundo Deportivo. Barca's head of scouting, João Amaral, reportedly watched the 19-year-old against Bahia, with Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Atlético Madrid also among his admirers. The left-footed defender, who earned a call-up to Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil squad, has a transfer value of around €30 million and after Spurs previously had a €21 million offer for 80% of his economic rights rejected.

- Tottenham Hotspur will not pursue a move for free-agent Mauro Icardi, Football Insider has revealed. The 33-year-old striker has been available since leaving Galatasaray in July, but Spurs are wary of his wage demands and lack of Premier League experience. Serie A is considered the likeliest destination for the former Sampdoria, Inter Milan and PSG star, with Lazio among several interested Italian clubs.

- Roma are interested in signing free-agent Raphaël Guerreiro, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The 32-year-old Portugal international left back has re-emerged as an option for manager Gian Piero Gasperini as a natural left-footed alternative on the flank, while Olympiacos are also interested in the former Bayern Munich defender.

- Raphinha is keen to remain at Barcelona, with the club attempting to extend his contract beyond June 2028 and only an intervention from a Saudi Pro League side could derail discussions. (AS)

- Brighton & Hove Albion and Aston Villa are monitoring the development of Club Nacional center back Mauro Coronel, 18, who is out of contract in December. (TEAMtalk)

- Liverpool will look to Benfica right back Daniel Banjaqui, 18, if they don't seal a €55 million permanent move for Barcelona's Ronald Araujo after his loan expires. (Anfield Watch)

- Chelsea are tracking the performances of 21-year-old forward Conrad Harder at sister-club Strasbourg ahead of a potential future move. (TEAMtalk)

- The Red Bull group and Spanish club Getafe are keen on signing Chilean U20 international midfielder Vicente Vargas. (Matteo Moretto)

- Newcastle United will target a young center back and a right-sided forward in the January transfer window and beyond. (iNews)

- A scout from Manchester City was present to watch FC Porto midfielder Victor Froholdt against rivals Benfica. (Sport Witness)

- Barcelona intend to insert a €500 million exit clause in midfielder Marc Bernal's new contract. (Mundo Deportivo)

- Premier League side Hull City are interested in Frosinone winger Giorgi Kvernadze. (Nicolo Schira)

- Union Berlin are exploring a move for former Real Madrid defender David Alaba, 34, who is currently a free agent. (Ekrem Konur)

stories.headline: Ugo Ugochukwu celebrates Nigerian roots after winning FIA Formula 3 championship
stories.summary: Newly crowned FIA Formula 3 champion Ugo Ugochukwu says he is proud to represent his Nigerian heritage on the international stage, even though he races under the United States flag.
stories.body:
Newly crowned FIA Formula 3 champion Ugo Ugochukwu says he is proud to represent his Nigerian heritage on the international stage, even though he races under the United States flag.

Ugochukwu, whose mother is Nigerian supermodel Oluchi Onweagba-Orlandi, became the first American to win the FIA Formula 3 championship after finishing second in the season-ending Feature Race in Madrid earlier this month.

He said during a post-race interview on SuperSport that his Nigerian heritage is a matter of pride: "I think it's amazing. I'm super proud of my Nigerian roots, on my mom's side.

"For me, it makes me very proud every time I can get on the podium, get my name out there to everyone watching and supporting in Africa. That means a lot and hopefully I can be a good role model to all the kids who would like to have this dream as well."

The 19-year-old entered the final weekend 15 points behind Britain's Freddie Slater, but drew level before last Sunday's race after qualifying and Saturday's Sprint Race.

Starting second behind Finland's Tuukka Taponen, Ugochukwu held his position to the finish while Slater came home eighth. The result gave the Campos Racing driver the championship with 159 points, 14 clear of Slater.

"There was a little bit of pressure, which is pretty normal," he said while describing the championship decider. "This last weekend was definitely the most important one of the championship."

With the hard part done in qualifying, the Ugochukwu said his priority in the final race was to protect the position he needed to secure the title, instead of chasing Taponen for the victory and putting it all at risk.

"We knew that was what I needed to win the championship, so it was just about getting it home," he said.

The championship win has attracted even more attention in Nigeria, where his maternal heritage means that Nigerians have followed his progress through the international racing ranks, all the way from his go-carting beginnings.

Born in New York to Onweagba-Orlandi and Italian fashion designer Luca Orlandi, Ugochukwu represents the United States in international competition. His mother won the inaugural M-Net Face of Africa competition in 1998 before going on to an international modelling career that included work with some of the world's leading fashion houses.

This Nigerian connection has previously brought public recognition from prominent Nigerians. After he won the Macau Grand Prix in 2024, Nigerians in Diaspora Commission Chair Abike Dabiri-Erewa congratulated him, while former presidential candidate Peter Obi also celebrated the achievement, pointing to his Nigerian heritage.

That Macau victory made Ugochukwu the first American to win the event since Bob Earl in 1981 and added to a record that already included the 2020 FIA Karting European Championship junior title and the inaugural Euro 4 Championship in 2023.

He added the Formula Regional Oceania championship earlier this year before returning for his second season in Formula 3.

His first F3 campaign with PREMA Racing in 2025 produced two podium finishes and 16th place in the championship. Now, the move to Campos Racing for 2026 has brought an immediate improvement, beginning with victory in the opening Feature Race in Melbourne.

Ugochukwu also won the Sprint Race at Silverstone and finished the season with two victories and seven podiums on his way to the title.

"This was the main goal at the start of the year, to get the championship," he said after Sunday's race. "I think after quali we knew we did our job, we did the main task, and today, and yesterday, it was just about execution and getting the points and bringing it home."

The title also drew congratulations from seven-time Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton, who visited with the young champ and acknowledged his achievement on Instagram.

Ugochukwu was part of McLaren's driver development program from the age of 13, when the Formula One team signed him to a long-term agreement following his success in karting.

The FIA Formula 3 Championship, which sits immediately below Formula 2, is on the principal development ladder to Formula One, with recent champions Oscar Piastri and Gabriel Bortoleto among those who subsequently progressed to F1.

The Liberty are 13-6 in conference games. New York ranks eighth in the WNBA with 38.7 points in the paint led by Breanna Stewart averaging 11.7.

The teams play for the third time this season. The Dream won the last matchup 95-84 on Sept. 22. Jordin Canada scored 19 points to help lead the Dream to the win.

stories.headline: Jones takes responsibility for Steveson leaving Octagon early
stories.summary: Jon Jones took responsibility for Gable Steveson's quick exit after a historic upset on Saturday, saying his instant reaction was to "get my friend to the back to make sure he was OK."
stories.body:
Gable Steveson, one of the biggest prospects in MMA history, has received a lot of criticism for immediately leaving the Octagon following his first professional loss Saturday in Los Angeles.

On Monday, Steveson's mentor and UFC legend Jon Jones took responsibility for Steveson's quick exit.

"I've seen some reports online and I really wanted to clear the air," Jones wrote on X. "It was my decision to take Gable straight to the back after the fight. Honestly it was the first time in this situation for me and my instant reaction was to get my friend to the back to make sure he was OK. Gable's work ethic and will to win is there and I stand by him and believe he will go on to be one of the best heavyweights in the UFC.

"He will be back I'm sure of it."

UFC commentator Daniel Cormier was among Steveson's critics after he left the Octagon, saying, "You cannot be a great winner but then an ungrateful loser, and I think that was bad by Steveson."

Sean Sharaf, who authored the monumental upset Saturday, said he wasn't greatly bothered by Steveson leaving early. Sharaf also told ESPN he expects the UFC to eventually book a rematch, given the history that was made in their first meeting.

"I know [the UFC] is going to want it," Sharaf said. "I already know the storyline, how it plays out, but I don't know. I think he's got to go do some reflecting and figure his stuff out because you can't underestimate anyone in this game no matter what. It's fighting and anything's possible."

An Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, Steveson (4-1) suffered one of the biggest upsets in UFC history -- and in shocking fashion. Sharaf (4-2), who was 0-2 in the organization going into UFC 331 at Crypto.com Arena, knocked out Steveson with a left hook just 12 seconds into their main card matchup. It was the third-fastest knockout in UFC heavyweight history.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

This is it, the weekend when we decide the two teams that will battle it out for the 2026 NRL premiership, and we have been presented with two cracking games to determine the grand finalists. On Friday night we have an attacking masterpiece when the Dolphins host the Roosters, before Sunday sees the giant-killing Knights facing the biggest giant of them all.

Good luck with your tips.
