Prediction: The Dolphins were very impressive two weeks ago against the Warriors, restricting them to one try, before unleashing their signature attacking blitz after the break. Previously this season they have allowed teams to get away to big head starts before mounting their fightback, a ploy which just won't stand up in the finals. They appear to have taken note and their defensive work in New Zealand was outstanding. They will need to be at their very best once more against the Roosters, who have the attacking flair to cause them plenty of problems.

The Roosters were simply too good for the Sharks last week, after going very close to beating the Panthers the week before. They have plenty of experience across the park, with Daly Cherry-Evans putting in a much better performance against the Sharks in combination with the hard running Hugo Savala. Outside those two, the Roosters backline bristles with attacking weapons, with Robert Toia and Mark Nawaqanitawase in unstoppable form, James Tedesco always lurking, and Sam Walker returning at halfback.

But, as we all know, the backs don't win the big games, they just determine the score, and the Roosters have a pack that is the match of any in the league. Naufahu Whyte, Lindsay Collins and Siua Wong were at their destructive best against the Sharks. Add the menace of Victor Radley and Spencer Leniu, plus the returning Angus Crichton, and there isn't a weakness across the middle or on the edges.

The Dolphins will have to match the Roosters forwards, with Thomas Flegler, Tom Gilbert, Max Plath, Kulikefu Finefeuiaki, Ray Stone and Francis Molo all in for a big night. If they can negate the Roosters pack, we all know how devastating the Dolphins halves and backs can be.

On paper this is very difficult to pick. It is one of those games that might come down to a key error, a moment of madness, the luck of the bounce or the whims of the referee's six again calls. Whoever wins, we are sure to be treated to an entertaining clash.

Prediction: The best team of the 2026 season meets the hottest team of the 2026 finals in what should be another great game in front of a large crowd in Homebush.

The Panthers didn't have it all their way two weeks ago when defeating the Roosters, they were well-matched and needed a wobbly Nathan Cleary field goal to break a late deadlock. Cleary has been the focus ever since, as first he avoided suspension for a dangerous contact charge, and then set about rehabilitating an injured foot. The Panthers have proven they can win games without Cleary, but his coolness under pressure is invaluable in the biggest games.

The Knights are playing with the casino's money at this stage. After finishing last in 2025, making the finals surpassed anyone's expectations. To be playing in the Preliminary Final is an incredible achievement for coach Justin Holbrook and his team, especially considering they are without star half Dylan Brown. They simply have to keep playing the way they have been playing. Fast moving defence, free flowing ball movement from anywhere on the field, and total belief in their ability to beat anyone. Phoenix Crossland, Fletcher Sharpe, Kalyn Ponga, Bradman Best, Dan Gagai, Dom Young, the Knights have weapons across the field. Without Jacob Saifiti, they are a little light on up front, but veteran Tyson Frizell has stepped up in the middle and the Knights back-row ranks, strengthened now by the surprise return of Dylan Lucas, have been simply brilliant.

The big question is; can the Knights execute their attacking style against the best defence in the business? They played just the once this season, with the Panthers winning 44-12. We know how good the Panthers are. We have seen them dominate the big games for years. Cleary and Dylan Edwards orchestrating the attack, Isaah Yeo and Liam Martin leading the defence. The Panthers are the best team in the competition for good reason and they stand between the other three teams and the premiership title. I think they'll return to the big dance this year.

stories.headline: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 3
stories.summary: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up ahead of Week 3? Plus, what we know for sure about the starting QBs around the league.
stories.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season marked a return to defensive dominance one week after record scoring numbers. This season, NFL defenses have a 35% pressure percentage (the highest through two weeks since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009) and a 25% pass rush rush win rate (highest since 2017).

How is this impacting quarterbacks around the league? In our Power Rankings ahead of Week 3, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to name the one thing we've learned so far from each team's QB situation. Which quarterbacks are handling the pressure? How are teams such as the Giants, Bears, Commanders, Seahawks and Vikings dealing with early injuries to their QB1s?

To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. And here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

The 49ers climbed into the top three, led by a near-perfect two weeks from quarterback Brock Purdy. He became the fifth QB in NFL history to record multiple games with 90% completion percentage, per ESPN Research. And San Francisco gets to stay at home for two more weeks, starting with the Cardinals next Sunday.
The Chargers are down to No. 22 after falling to 0-2. According to ESPN Research, they are the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to be favored by at least 6.5 points in each of their first two games and lose both. The Raiders, who most recently beat the Chargers, are at No. 20 and 2-0 for the first time since 2021.
Meanwhile, the Falcons and Dolphins are squarely at the bottom of the rankings. The Dolphins are the only team to not lead at any point this season, and ESPN's Football Power Index already gives them a 43% chance at the No. 1 pick. Atlanta is hoping to rebound with quarterback Michael Penix Jr. back in the fold from ACL surgery.

Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team as last week.

Jump to a team:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

1. Buffalo Bills (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Lions 41-31

Week 2 ranking: 1

One thing we know about the QB1: Josh Allen is going to make defenses pay either way.

Allen has kept his eyes downfield through two games, averaging a career-best 9.7 yards per attempt on his deepest average depth of target (10.5) since 2018, his rookie season. That has led to three touchdowns on throws of 20-plus air yards. But Allen is just as dangerous when defenses bail out to protect against the deep ball. Of his 92 rushing yards on 20 carries this season, 70 have come on six scramble plays. -- Nick Suss

2. Seattle Seahawks (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Cardinals 31-7

Week 2 ranking: 2

One thing we know about the QB1: Drew Lock is one of the NFL's best backup QBs.

He's not the same player who turned the ball over 25 times in 24 games over his first three seasons in Denver. Or the one who couldn't beat out Geno Smith after a trade to Seattle in 2022. Lock has gotten plenty of help from receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Seattle's defense, but he has also played like a starter. Since stepping in for an injured Sam Darnold one series into the season opener, Lock has completed almost 73% of his passes with four touchdowns, zero turnovers and only two sacks. His Total QBR of 86.4 ranks fourth. -- Brady Henderson

3. San Francisco 49ers (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Dolphins 35-13

Week 2 ranking: 5

One thing we know about the QB1: Brock Purdy looks poised for his best season.

Purdy has been one of the league's most productive quarterbacks since taking over the starting job in 2022. Now in his fifth season, he's completely comfortable in coach Kyle Shanahan's offense and coming off his best training camp. That hot start has teammates such as linebacker Fred Warner openly wondering whether Purdy can compete for league MVP honors. Through two weeks, Purdy is atop the league in QBR (94.9) despite a supporting cast that has already been thinned by injury. If he stays healthy, there's reason to believe Purdy will post his best year yet. -- Nick Wagoner

4. Kansas City Chiefs (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Colts 33-30 (OT)

Week 2 ranking: 8

One thing we know about the QB1: Patrick Mahomes can deal from under center.

With the addition of running back Kenneth Walker III, Mahomes has shown that he can be surgical when passing from under center, especially on play-action passes. On under-center plays, Mahomes threw a touchdown against the Colts and has already recorded 107 passing yards. It's one of the biggest changes from last season, when the clear majority of the Chiefs' snaps with Mahomes were in the shotgun -- 80.6% of their formations (excluding quarterback kneel-downs), third most in the league. -- Nate Taylor

5. Los Angeles Rams (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Giants 28-6

Week 2 ranking: 4

One thing we know about the QB1: Matthew Stafford is still capable of playing at an MVP level.

Stafford and the Rams' offense struggled in the season opener, but wide receiver Davante Adams said the team's Week 2 offensive performance was closer to what the group expects to look like this season. On Monday night against the Giants, Stafford, the reigning MVP, completed 22 of 31 passes for 327 yards with four touchdown passes and an interception. He had that success without wide receiver Puka Nacua, who is dealing with soreness in his groin. -- Sarah Barshop

6. Philadelphia Eagles (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Titans 24-20

Week 2 ranking: 6

One thing we know about the QB1: Jalen Hurts is carrying this team.

The thought heading into the season was Hurts and the passing offense would need time to acclimate to coordinator Sean Mannion's system, meaning the Eagles would have to rely on their defense and ground game early. The defense did not dominate as expected against Washington and Tennessee, while the running game has been spotty behind an offensive line still trying to find its footing. Meanwhile, Hurts led the team to a Week 1 win with three touchdowns and another victory Sunday via a go-ahead touchdown drive in the closing seconds. He is tied for second in touchdown passes (five) and ahead of schedule in this new scheme. -- Tim McManus

7. Baltimore Ravens (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Saints 24-17

Week 2 ranking: 3

One thing we know about the QB1: Lamar Jackson is facing a lot of pressure.

Baltimore's revamped offensive line has struggled in protection. The Ravens' two lowest pass block win rates with Jackson as the starting QB have come in the first two weeks this season. Baltimore had a 38% pass block win rate at the Colts in Week 1 and a 33% win rate in Week 2. Jackson and the Ravens should have a more favorable matchup this week against the Cowboys, who have two sacks this season. -- Jamison Hensley

8. Denver Broncos (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Jaguars 20-13

Week 2 ranking: 9

One thing we know about the QB1: Bo Nix might not be all that fond of September.

Whether it's an issue with his mechanics or rushing into plays, Nix is caught up in the Broncos' propensity for slow starts under coach Sean Payton. In his first two seasons, Nix has thrown eight of his 23 interceptions in September -- including three games with at least two picks. And in the season-opening loss to the Chiefs, Nix had his first career three-fumble game and was sacked four times, tying a career high. The Broncos escaped with a win in Week 2 after Nix and the offense got things cranked up in the second half. But he did throw his second interception of the season. -- Jeff Legwold

9. Cincinnati Bengals (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Texans 20-6

Week 2 ranking: 15

One thing we know about the QB1: Joe Burrow is a tough customer.

In reality, the back injury he had going into Week 2 wasn't particularly severe. But it was still an example of Burrow's toughness that his teammates appreciate. And despite the injury and getting sacked five times against Houston, he made all the necessary plays to steer the Bengals to their first 2-0 start with him as a healthy quarterback. Burrow has also been clutch. He ranks 10th in the league in third-down QBR (86.1), according to ESPN Research. And he has a near-perfect red zone QBR through two games (99.9). -- Ben Baby

10. New England Patriots (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Steelers 20-3

Week 2 ranking: 10

One thing we know about the QB1: Drake Maye's accuracy isn't what he's accustomed to.

After leading the NFL with a 72% completion percentage in 2025, Maye has completed 67.3% of his throws through two games -- with one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Those performances came against two of the league's top defenses (Seahawks and Steelers), but Maye isn't satisfied with his performance. "It starts with me making good decisions, being in good plays," he said. -- Mike Reiss

11. Chicago Bears (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Vikings 9-3

Week 2 ranking: 7

One thing we know about the QB1: Caleb Williams' hamstring injury isn't serious.

The Bears dodged a major bullet with the right hamstring injury Williams sustained late against the Vikings. Coach Ben Johnson labeled Williams as week-to-week, and while the QB is expected to miss some time, Johnson is confident that backup Tyson Bagent can operate the offense. It understandably won't look the same as when Williams is under center, but the scheme will not change. Chicago gave Bagent a two-year, $10 million extension in 2025, and his experience with Johnson in preseason games is why the coach believes "we'll be fine." -- Courtney Cronin

12. Minnesota Vikings (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Bears 9-3

Week 2 ranking: 17

One thing we know about the QB1: The Vikings can win with replacement-level QB play.

Starter Kyler Murray (concussion) hasn't played since the Vikings' 11th offensive play, and Carson Wentz has produced a typical backup performance. Wentz ranks 22nd in the NFL in QBR (52.0) and 29th in completion percentage (58%), and he's tied for the seventh-most sacks (six). However, the Vikings are undefeated on the strength of everything but their passing game. Their defense and special teams both rank No. 6 in the NFL in EPA, while their rushing game ranks No. 16 in EPA. That's a good sign for the entire team with Murray returning this week. -- Kevin Seifert

13. Jacksonville Jaguars (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Broncos 20-13

Week 2 ranking: 13

One thing we know about the QB1: Trevor Lawrence has to be better against pressure.

The difference is stark for Lawrence this season. When he's not under pressure, he's completing 76.9% of his passes (11th in the NFL) for three touchdowns to one interception. When he's under pressure, he's completing only 38.5% of his passes with one TD. Jacksonville's offensive line struggled against Denver, and if that becomes a seasonlong issue, Lawrence is going to have to be more efficient under pressure. He won't face easy defensive fronts over the next month, either. -- Michael DiRocco

14. Detroit Lions (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Bills 41-31

Week 2 ranking: 12

One thing we know about the QB1: Jared Goff continues to build a case the greatest QB in franchise history.

Despite facing heavy pressure behind a banged-up offensive line, Goff has continued his efficient play in Year 11. He has racked up 25 straight games with a passing touchdown, which is the longest active streak in NFL and the longest in Lions history, per ESPN Research. He also reached 40,000 career yards in Buffalo, tying Kirk Cousins and Dan Marino as the fourth-fastest to that mark in NFL history (153 games). Goff is currently in his sixth season in Detroit and continues to reach major milestones at 31 years old. -- Eric Woodyard

15. Houston Texans (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Bengals 20-6

Week 2 ranking: 11

One thing we know about the QB1: C.J. Stroud just needs a healthy supporting cast.

Stroud has thrown for 627 passing yards in the first two games, third most in the NFL, but that has led to only two touchdowns. The Texans didn't find the end zone at all in Week 2, as No. 1 option Nico Collins missed the game because of a hamstring injury. Stroud's play style isn't necessarily one that can consistently create explosive results when plays break down. He needs the players around him to be healthy so he can produce in structure. -- DJ Bien-Aime

16. Dallas Cowboys (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Commanders 37-20

Week 2 ranking: 16

One thing we know about the QB1: The Cowboys will go as far as Dak Prescott can take them.

There have been -- and will be -- growing pains with the defense, so a lot will be on Prescott's plate. The run game has not been what the Cowboys have wanted so far, either. Through two games, Prescott is completing 73.8% of his passes, and he has been able to escape harm with his legs, too. He has six touchdown passes and one interception, but the one giveaway shows the Cowboys' thin margin for error. The Giants turned that into a touchdown to shift the momentum in Dallas' Week 1 loss. -- Todd Archer

17. Green Bay Packers (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Jets 20-17 (OT)

Week 2 ranking: 14

One thing we know about the QB1: Jordan Love is getting hit ... a lot.

Through two games, Love has taken 18 quarterback hits and been sacked four times. And given the state of his offensive line, it might not get much better anytime soon. The Packers lost right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele and their top two left guards, starter Aaron Banks and backup Donovan Jennings, on Sunday. Regardless, Green Bay still avoided its first 0-2 start since 2006, keeping alive the longest active streak in the NFL, per ESPN Research. -- Rob Demovsky

18. New York Giants (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Rams 28-6

Week 2 ranking: 18

One thing we know about the QB1: It's all about Jaxson Dart staying on the field.

The young quarterback looked tremendous in Week 1, especially from the pocket, where he had a QBR of 91.0. But Dart got injured on the opening drive Monday night against the Rams and backup Jameis Winston struggled. Winston's accuracy was a problem. In the first half alone, he completed 5 of 12 passes with an overthrown screen and open rollout in the red zone among the misses. It never got better. The Giants' offense didn't look the same without Dart's running threat. Winston had two rushes for 1 yard in the contest. -- Jordan Raanan

19. New Orleans Saints (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Ravens 24-17

Week 2 ranking: 25

One thing we know about the QB1: Tyler Shough can handle the big moments, but he needs to start faster.

Shough has had two up-and-down games to start the season, but he has been at his best in the fourth quarter, which led to a comeback win against the Ravens. According to ESPN Research, Shough has a 14.3 Total QBR in the opening three quarters of games (29th among 30 qualifying passers this season). In fourth quarters and overtime, he ranks second with a 97.7 QBR. Shough is also 5-of-5 for 127 yards and a touchdown on passes of 15-plus air yards in fourth quarters. -- Katherine Terrell

20. Las Vegas Raiders (2-0)
Week 2 result: Beat the Chargers 26-14

Week 2 ranking: 28

One thing we know about the QB1: Kirk Cousins can handle pressure well.

Cousins has been pressured on 36.5% of his dropbacks through two games. In those situations, he has completed 13 of 21 passes (61.9%) for 161 yards, three touchdowns, an interception and a passer rating of 105.6. Against the Chargers, Cousins was pressured on 40.6% of his dropbacks. Yet he still managed to throw for 108 yards and two scores whenever the Chargers brought the heat. -- Ryan McFadden

21. Carolina Panthers (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Falcons 34-3

Week 2 ranking: 26

One thing we know about the QB1: Bryce Young isn't afraid to throw it deep.

Young averaged 5.6 yards per dropback over the past two seasons. He is averaging 8.0 yards in 2026, which ranks fifth. On Sunday, Young completed 8 of 11 passes for 197 yards and a touchdown on throws beyond 10 yards. Against the Bears in Week 1, Young threw for a career-high 221 yards on throws beyond 10 yards. Young is also sharing the wealth among his targets, as wide receivers Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan each have a 100-yard receiving performance this season. -- Mike Kaye

22. Los Angeles Chargers (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Raiders 26-14

Week 2 ranking: 19

One thing we know about the QB1: Justin Herbert looks uncomfortable.

For the past two Sundays, this Chargers' offense has looked like a unit that hadn't practiced together before. Herbert looks lost and, at moments, angrier than he has ever been at the helm of a flat offense. He had three fumbles (all recovered) and two interceptions Sunday, though one was because of a dropped pass by tight end David Njoku. This new offense under coordinator Mike McDaniel was supposed to elevate this team into a championship contender. Instead, its star quarterback looks almost unrecognizable. -- Kris Rhim

23. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Browns 23-19

Week 2 ranking: 20

One thing we know about the QB1: Baker Mayfield is full healthy, but something is not right.

The Bucs returned their entire starting offensive line, they boast a receivers room that would make many teams envious, and running back Bucky Irving is averaging more than 5.0 yards per carry. But Mayfield has turned the ball over four times, has not been accurate and seems lost without franchise scoring leader Mike Evans at receiver. Mayfield had similar struggles last season when Evans was on the injury report for 10 weeks. Now, Mayfield is struggling. -- Jenna Laine

24. Indianapolis Colts (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Chiefs 33-30 (OT)

Week 2 ranking: 22

One thing we know about the QB1: Daniel Jones' Achilles injury is not impeding him.

The Colts' record doesn't scream "great QB play," but Jones has mostly done his part. In Week 2, he showed the full gamut of his game in spite of his recently healed Achilles tear. He helped bring the Colts back from a deficit, scrambled, took a couple brutal hits and stretched the field when he could. Jones is completing 66.1% of his pass attempts, making the most of an offense that is being sabotaged by an inept defense. -- Stephen Holder

25. Pittsburgh Steelers (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Patriots 20-3

Week 2 ranking: 21

One thing we know about the QB1: Aaron Rodgers is no longer comfortable under pressure.

So far this season, Rodgers has completed just 8 of 24 attempts on 31 dropbacks under pressure. He has been sacked six times on such plays. Rodgers is also completing a career-low 50% against the blitz, as his off-target percentage on such throws is a career-worst 30.4%. While the offensive line's struggles have significantly contributed to Rodgers' inaccuracy, his decreased mobility at 42 years old has made it even more difficult to manage the pressure. -- Brooke Pryor

26. Arizona Cardinals (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Seahawks 31-7

Week 2 ranking: 24

One thing we know about the QB1: Jacoby Brissett should be just fine.

The first two weeks have already been a roller coaster for Brissett, who threw for 277 yards in Week 1 but only 95 on Sunday against the defending Super Bowl champions. His body of work since he became Arizona's starter in Week 6 last season is solid. He ranks No. 1 in completions and attempts, No. 2 in passing yards, No. 4 in completion percentage over expected and No. 5 in passing touchdowns. His performance Sunday was vastly different than the last time he played Seattle, when he threw for 258 yards and two touchdowns in a blowout loss in Week 10 last season. -- Josh Weinfuss

27. New York Jets (1-1)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Packers 20-17 (OT)

Week 2 ranking: 27

One thing we know about the QB1: Look, no interceptions for Geno Smith.

This is notable because Smith threw a league-high 17 interceptions last season with the Raiders. He's making smart decisions with the ball for the most part -- not a single turnover in 74 dropbacks. He's completing nearly 71% of his passes, though he's averaging only 5.8 air yards per attempt -- tied with Daniel Jones for 28th in the league. Going forward, the Jets need to open up the passing attack to maximize their skill-position talent. -- Rich Cimini

28. Washington Commanders (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Cowboys 37-20

Week 2 ranking: 23

One thing we know about the QB1: Jayden Daniels can't stay healthy.

Daniels has now left because of an injury in four of his past five games -- three times because of his left elbow. He has dislocated it twice, including Sunday in Dallas, and reinjured it when he returned last season. The shame of it is the comment before the injury would've been that Daniels is back. He had a strong finish in the Commanders' season-opening loss to the Eagles and was playing well in Dallas. With a healthy Daniels, Washington is a much different threat. But he just has to ... stay healthy. -- John Keim

29. Cleveland Browns (1-1)
Week 2 result: Beat the Buccaneers 23-19

Week 2 ranking: 32

One thing we know about the QB1: Deshaun Watson found a risk-averse winning formula.

In Week 2, Watson earned his first win since September 2024 with the lowest average depth of target (3.7) of his career. At times, it has seemed like the Browns' passing game has been played in a phone booth: Watson's 6.7 air yards per attempt would tie a career low. However, the play style has limited turnover potential and allowed the Browns' young playmakers to get the ball in their hands. Cleveland ranks third in yards after the catch (260) through two games. -- Daniel Oyefusi

30. Tennessee Titans (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Eagles 24-20

Week 2 ranking: 30

One thing we know about the QB1: Cam Ward will run the ball more this season.

Ward isn't a major threat to defenses with his legs, but he has become more effective at it. He picked up a couple of early first downs in the Week 1 loss to the Jets. And he was even more effective Sunday, rushing for two touchdowns to become the fifth Titans/Oilers quarterback in 50 seasons to run for multiple touchdowns in a game. Coordinator Brian Daboll has always encouraged his quarterbacks to run when necessary. Now it's Ward's turn. -- Turron Davenport

31. Atlanta Falcons (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the Panthers 34-3

Week 2 ranking: 29

One thing we know about the QB1: The Falcons are desperate for Michael Penix Jr.

There are a handful of statistics that exemplify the historic futility of the Falcons' offense under third-string quarterback Cooper Rush. But none are better than this: Atlanta is the fourth team since NFL play-by-play was first tracked in 1978 without a red zone drive through two games -- and the first in 18 seasons. With three straight primetime games, the Falcons badly need Penix to be back to old self quickly. Thursday against the Packers will mark his first start since tearing his ACL last November. -- Marc Raimondi

32. Miami Dolphins (0-2)
Week 2 result: Lost to the 49ers 35-13

Week 2 ranking: 31

One thing we know about the QB1: Malik Willis is still developing -- and needs more help.

Willis hasn't been the issue for the Dolphins' offense, but he's clearly adjusting to a new scheme and new teammates. On one hand, Miami's receivers room consists of three rookies and has struggled to consistently get open. Willis has also been sacked at the highest rate in the NFL. But at the same time, his completion percentage over expectation of minus-3.5% ranks fourth worst in the NFL, per NFL Next Gen Stats, and there have been plays in which here he refused to hit his checkdowns. Miami believes in Willis, and a learning curve is expected considering his limited starting experience. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

stories.headline: Wayne Rooney: 'Disappointing' if 'top player' JJ Gabriel leaves Man United
stories.summary: Wayne Rooney has said it would be "disappointing" for Manchester United to lose "special talent" JJ Gabriel.
stories.body:
Wayne Rooney has said it would be "disappointing" for Manchester United to lose "special talent" JJ Gabriel.

Gabriel, 15, asked to leave United and Barcelona and Real Madrid are among the clubs monitoring his situation, sources told ESPN.

He turns 16 next month and recently shone on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah by scoring a hat trick.

"I have seen JJ grow up, he has been in [my son] Kai's team," Wayne Rooney told Stick To Football on Disney+. "Anyone close to it knew that was coming.

"In fairness to Manchester United they have done everything, absolutely everything, to keep him at the club.

"The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special player. I know, I recognise that, because I was that player at Everton. I was getting that treatment at Everton.

"As a club, you need to do [it] to try to keep the better players.

"It's disappointing because he is such a top player and a lovely kid.

"You never know whether it's gone too far or whether there is a chance for him to stay."

United believe they could rectify the issue, sources previously told ESPN.

- Why Man United's wantaway 15-year-old wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated

- Transfer rumors, news: Mesloub to replace Gabriel at Man United?

- Harry Maguire: Man United didn't take chances against Fulham, paid the price

Rooney became the Premier League's youngest goalscorer when he struck for Everton aged 16 years and 360 days old in 2002. That record is now held by Arsenal's Max Dowman after he scored against Everton in March aged 16 years and 73 days.

Rooney became a United and England legend and now sees an exciting talent within Gabriel.

"He is a top player," Rooney said of the 15-year-old. "His ability, his balance, he has shown he can go up the ages and score goals. The next step is first-team football where it's different, and you never know until you're in there.

"But he's such a special talent who understands the game really well.

"At some point this season he would [have] made his debut for the first-team, I'd imagine, so that's where it's disappointing."

stories.headline: Isack Hadjar returns to Red Bull for Azerbaijan GP after injury layoff
stories.summary: Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar will return to action at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing the last three races with a wrist injury.
stories.body:
Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar will return to action at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing the last three races with a wrist injury.

The French driver injured his wrist while training during Formula 1's August break and was ruled out of the Dutch, Italian and Spanish Grands Prix as a result.

Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson substituted for Hadjar at all three races, while reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson's place at the junior Red Bull team.

Hadjar's return at Red Bull means Lawson will now resume his season at Racing Bulls, with Tsunoda continuing on the sidelines as a potential stand-in for the rest of the season.

"Oracle Red Bull Racing is delighted to welcome Isack back this weekend," a Red Bull statement said. "Having made a successful recovery from his wrist injury, Isack will return to action at the Baku City Circuit on Thursday.

"The team would like to sincerely thank Liam for his professionalism, dedication and hard work over the past three races. Stepping in under challenging circumstances, he delivered some impressive performances and made a valuable contribution to the team. We wish him all the very best as he returns to Visa Cash App Racing Bulls."

Lawson scored 14 points across the three rounds he was driving alongside Max Verstappen at Red Bull, bringing his total points tally to 59 for the season.

While sitting out of the last three rounds, Hadjar had his one and only podium of the season reinstated by the FIA's International Court of Appeal after it overruled Alpine's right of review over the result of the Monaco Grand Prix earlier in the season.

The UFC's heavyweight division appears to be stuck in neutral gear.

It's not just about Tom Aspinall vacating the championship on Monday because he is still recovering from an eye injury suffered in last October's no-contest in a title defense against Ciryl Gane. The top 10 still features Aspinall -- he's eligible to be ranked until the middle of next month, when he will have been inactive for a year -- and includes two heavyweights from outside the UFC in the top six (Francis Ngannou, Vadim Nemkov).

Cortes Acosta entered the weekend ranked sixth, but after losing by unanimous decision, he drops to No. 9. Blaydes is one spot above him, moving up from 10th.

The only other movement in the divisional rankings is at women's flyweight, where former UFC champion Alexa Grasso moves up one position to No. 4 after Saturday's unanimous decision win over Manon Fiorot. Formerly ranked second, Fiorot drops three spots after her first loss in a nontitle bout since her pro debut in 2018.

stories.headline: Daicos backs Neale to beat ban and play in Grand Final
stories.summary: Collingwood superstar Nick Daicos wants his fellow Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale to be cleared of suspension to play in the AFL Grand Final.
stories.body:
Newly-crowned Brownlow medallist Nick Daicos is hopeful Brisbane Lions star Lachie Neale's suspension can be overturned and he will be free to play in the AFL Grand Final.

Neale and the Lions on Tuesday night will challenge at the AFL tribunal a one-match ban offered to the two-time Brownlow medal winner.

If the suspension is upheld, Neale will miss Saturday's Grand Final against Fremantle, his former club, at the MCG.

How Nick Daicos fared on Brownlow night vs. ESPN's predictor

It is widely expected Neale will leave the Lions in the off-season and join Daicos at Collingwood on a bumper three-year deal.

Neale would provide invaluable support to Daicos in a midfield that was regularly held up by the Magpies maestro's class.

"Absolutely," Daicos said on Tuesday when asked if Neale should be free to play.

"You want to see the best players out there.

"Lachie's clearly proven himself over the last 15 years as one of the greats of the competition.

"I'd love to see him out there, and I think it's going to be a ripping game.

"You want to see the best players out there."

Neale has been charged with striking Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan in Saturday night's preliminary final.

Neale's gut punch on Ginnivan was graded as intentional conduct, medium impact and body contact by match review officer Michael Christian.

With damning vision showing Neale guilty of the behind-play strike, and numerous precedents this season of other players being banned for one match for similar strikes, the Lions are set to argue the suspension should be downgraded to a fine.

Brisbane will cite a fresh clause that allowed Collingwood great Scott Pendlebury to avoid a suspension in March.

Pendlebury was given a one-game ban for rough conduct for a bump on Adelaide's Josh Worrell.

He was found guilty by the tribunal but the sanction was downgraded to a $3000 fine due to "compelling and exceptional circumstances" - a clause open to the tribunal that will be central to Neale's case.

The relevant clause states: "Players will not automatically receive a reduced sanction for a good record.

"However, if a classifiable offence is contested or referred to the tribunal, a player with an exemplary record may argue that their good record constitutes exceptional and compelling circumstances".

The Magpies successfully argued that clause applied to Pendlebury, who had never previously faced the tribunal in his storied 21-year career.

Neale also has not previously fronted the tribunal in a 320-game career. He is also a dual Brownlow medallist and premiership captain, plus a four-time All Australian and four-time club champion.

Geelong coach Chris Scott does not agree with the provision.

"Seriously, when we're starting to say, 'There's a rule for you because you've done good things for the game', it's almost implying that other people haven't done a good job," Scott said on AFL360.

He added, however: "I know his record is exceptional, but aside from that, I just like to see them play."

Scott added that the AFL could not have been more clear about their crackdown on gut punches.

Meanwhile, Neale's teammates are not yet dwelling on the possibility of losing the star on-baller for the premiership decider against his old team Fremantle.

"Talk about adversity, one of our best traits is being able to deal with that," Lion Jarrod Berry said.

"We do it well and there's no point putting energy into it until we know the result.

"We'll be sitting tight and praying that he gets off. But if he doesn't, we'll face it when it comes."

If the ban stands, Brisbane could take the case to the AFL Appeals Board in a last-ditch effort.

stories.headline: Dreyer outduels Messi as San Diego hands Miami 4th straight draw
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.

It was Inter Miami's fourth consecutive draw in MLS play as new manager Kily González oversaw his first league game in charge of the club and cut a frustrated figure after conceding a late goal to drop points.

"We've been here for four days and haven't been able to train properly. Defensively, we really need to be much stronger," González said after the game. "We can't commit these defensive horrors, they come at a high cost. That final situation shouldn't have happened. It's surreal to be in a position to win the game, yet nearly lose it.

"We only avoided defeat because our goalkeeper saved us."

Dreyer gave San Diego a 1-0 lead in the 12th minute, capitalizing on a through ball from Jeppe Tverskov before deftly chipping over goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

Messi answered in the 24th with his 20th league goal of the season. His free kick from the right side went untouched through the penalty area and into the far side of the net, four days after he scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in a 2-0 win over Mexican side Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup.

"I think the Campeones Cup might have had an unconscious effect, especially in the first half, leading to a bit of complacency," González added. "These are factors that are part of football. At a club where we are obliged to win every match we play, we have to rise to the occasion. We made significant adjustments at halftime to get the team flowing and ensure we stayed compact, keeping the lines tight so we wouldn't suffer the way we did in the first half."

The goal was Messi's eighth from a free kick since entering the league in 2023, more than any other player in MLS during that time span.

Luis Suárez put Miami ahead in the 74th minute as Miami looked set to leapfrog New England into second place in the Eastern Conference, but Dreyer scored his second of the night eight minutes later with another fine finish -- this time from a ball over the top of the Herons' backline.

Miami is now in third place with a record of 12-4-10 with 46 points -- 11 behind first-place Nashville.

"But anyway, we have to keep going," González said. "On the positive side, we did some good things, but I need to fine-tune the defensive side because that's what really worries me most."

Earlier Sunday, FIFA announced that the final phase of the 2027 FIFA Women's Champions Cup will be played at Inter Miami's home of Nu Stadium in January. FIFA Chief Football Officer Jill Ellis spoke at halftime about bringing the competition to Miami.

"I think we've seen that this city loves its football. We've seen it this past summer with the World Cup," Ellis said. "I think it's time to bring a major women's tournament here to Miami. I think it's exciting."

Miami returns to MLS play next Sunday on the road against the Columbus Crew, while San Diego is also on the road with a game against Austin FC on Saturday.

ESPN writer Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report, while information from The Associated Press was also used.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail preliminary finals: Yeo and Leota keen to stay Panthers
stories.summary: Isaah Yeo and Moses Leota are both keens to remain Panthers despite interest elsewhere, while Casey McLean is happy for his departing brother.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's preliminary finals weekend.

Yeo and Leota's future

Isaah Yeo has confirmed his preference is to remain at Penrith beyond his current contract, and is hoping to sort out his future following the end of the season.

"It always has been [my preference to stay]," Yeo admitted.

"The idea is to stay at Penrith as a one club player."

Moses Leota has also affirmed his love for Penrith, with the hope a deal gets done following the 2026 finals.

"[Remaining at Penrith] is massive to me," he shared.

"I've been here basically my whole life."

Casey McLean backs brother at Bulldogs

Panthers gun Casey McLean admitted while he's "gutted" that his brother Jesse will be leaving Penrith next year, but he's excited to see him flourish at Canterbury.

"Obviously pretty gutted that we won't be on the same team," he told ESPN.

"It'll be a weird feeling at first, but I'm super excited for the opportunity that he'll be given [at the Bulldogs]."

He went on to vouch for Jesse's ability on the field, expecting his older brother to remind fans of his talent.

"He does talk a little s--- on the field," Casey joked.

"But he's just an amazing player - he helped me grow as well.

"He's such an amazing role model, not only for myself, but for a fair few boys here as well."
